source.description: The source image location used to create a disk.

name.description: Name of the vm-disk to clone.

http.description: Download image from an HTTP source.

image.description: Use image by name from default collection.

name.description: Name of the image to use.

optical.description: Defines if disk should be considered optical.

storage.description: The size of the disk allocated for the virtual machine.

storageClass.description: StorageClass used to store the data.

bindImmediately.description: Provision the volume at disk creation instead of waiting for a consumer.

substrate.description: Which hypervisor holds the disk. `kubevirt` makes it a CDI DataVolume inside this cluster. `proxmox` makes it a volume on the external Proxmox VE cluster the platform's proxmox-vm package points at, kept on a per-namespace holder VM between uses, so that it outlives the VM it is attached to. A disk cannot move between substrates: the chart reads the live object and refuses to switch. On proxmox, `storageClass` names an entry of the platform's catalog rather than a Kubernetes StorageClass; `source.image.name` is one of the catalog's images or an image published in cozy-public as a cloneable VirtualMachineVolume (the vm-default-images package with substrate proxmox, or a disk the platform made cloneable), which has to live on the node of this disk; `source.disk.name` copies another vm-disk of this namespace on the same node; `source.http`, `source.upload` and `optical` are not available yet.

node.description: Proxmox node the volume is created on. A VM can only attach disks that live on its own node. Empty takes the catalog's default node.
